defaultPrompt:
[SUMMARY TOKEN LIMIT=
Language: English]

Create an information-dense summary of the roleplay using the sections below. Rebuild it every time from everything you are given: the historical context and the messages to replace. The summary describes the current state of the story, not a log of messages. It must contain enough information for the roleplay to continue naturally and consistently even if the original messages are no longer available.

INPUT=
- Text between <Historical_Context> and </Historical_Context> is earlier chat history. Use it as context; its oldest part may be cut off in long chats.
- The messages after </Historical_Context> are the ones this summary will replace.
- Earlier summaries may appear in either part. Treat them as established facts and carry their content forward.

BEFORE WRITING=
Before writing, go through the whole input, including early and middle messages (in your reasoning if you have one, otherwise silently, without writing the list), and list:
- every named character, including minor ones;
- every promise, agreement, debt and plan, and whether it was fulfilled;
- every secret, lie and misunderstanding, and who knows or believes what;
- every important object and who has it now;
- injuries, physical changes and how much time has passed;
- unresolved threads, including ones not mentioned recently.
Then compare the list against your draft and add anything missing. Do not include this checklist in the final summary.

OUTPUT RULES=
- Write the entire summary in English, regardless of the language of the chat history. Keep character names, place names and nicknames in the spelling used in the chat.
- Output only the summary. No preamble, commentary, or continuation of the story.
- Third person, compact sentences, no literary embellishment.
- Each fact goes in the single section where it fits best. Repeat information only when necessary for clarity.
- If a section has nothing to report, write "None".
- Do not invent details. Distinguish established facts from suspicions, assumptions and speculation, and mark the latter as such.
- Never give a character knowledge they did not acquire in the story.
- The current state of the story takes priority over obsolete temporary states.
- Prefer specific details over generalizations: names, numbers, dates, exact objects, exact terms of promises. Write "gave her a silver ring engraved with a moon", not "gave her a gift".
- Keep every open thread, promise, secret and possession until the chat explicitly resolves or changes it. Do not drop something just because it has not been mentioned recently.
- Keep named minor characters even if they appeared only once, with one line on who they are.
- Preserve cause and effect when it explains current behavior or circumstances.
- Completeness matters more than brevity. Use as much of the length limit as the story needs.
- If space runs short, shorten CONTINUITY DETAILS and RECENT first. Never drop SECRETS & KNOWLEDGE or OPEN THREADS.

[BEGINNING=
The initial scenario as shown in the first messages: setting and circumstances, characters present, initial relationships and dynamics, important conditions, conflicts and goals.]

[CURRENT SCENE=
Location and environment; time, date, weather or lighting when established; characters present and their positions when relevant; what each character is doing; the conversation or action in progress; what is about to happen.]

[RECENT=
Bullet points of events after the beginning that explain how the current situation came about: important actions and decisions, significant conversations and discoveries, their consequences, shared experiences, and small events that may affect future behavior. Skip events with no lasting relevance.]

[{{char}}=
- Appearance: current clothing, physical condition, injuries, possessions, and changes not already in the character description.
- Demeanor: current mood, attitude and emotional state.
- Goals: current intentions, plans, desires and motivations.]

[{{user}}=
- Appearance: current clothing, physical condition, injuries, possessions.
- Demeanor: current mood, attitude and emotional state when relevant.
- Goals: current intentions, plans, desires and motivations.]

[SIDE CHARACTERS=
For each relevant character, present or absent: who they are, current location or status, goals and involvement in the story, important knowledge they possess, meaningful changes that happened to them. Relationships go in RELATIONSHIPS.]

[RELATIONSHIPS=
{{char}} ↔ {{user}} first, then other important pairs. For each: trust or distrust; affection, attraction, attachment, resentment, fear, jealousy, dependence or other emotions; familiarity and comfort level; boundaries; how the relationship has changed and which events changed it; shared memories that matter; unresolved tensions; subtle dynamics that may affect future behavior even if never stated aloud.]

[CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT=
Lasting changes in beliefs, values, habits, fears, confidence, boundaries, worldview or behavior for each important character, and what caused them. New attachments or aversions. Behavioral patterns that emerged during the roleplay. Not temporary moods.]

[SECRETS & KNOWLEDGE=
Who knows what: secrets and who keeps them; information {{char}} knows that {{user}} does not, and the reverse; information known by side characters; information deliberately hidden from someone; suspicions; misunderstandings and false beliefs; important discoveries and who witnessed them.]

[OPEN THREADS=
Unresolved plots, mysteries, unanswered questions, conflicts, threats, investigations, unfinished conversations and decisions, plans, appointments, invitations, promises, debts and obligations. For each: who is involved, what exactly was agreed or is at stake, and current status.]

[IMPORTANT STRINGS=
Persistent facts: rules of the setting and world, significant locations, enemies and organizations, important objects and who holds them, permanent consequences of past events, rules and agreements between characters.]

[CONTINUITY DETAILS=
Small details that prevent contradictions: habits and mannerisms, speech patterns, nicknames and forms of address, preferences and dislikes, recurring jokes and references, small shared memories, details of rooms, routines and possessions. Only details with narrative, emotional or relational value.]
